checks: Since S is nonempty, the cover cardinalities lie in {1,…,N}. Take a constant-cardinality subsequence, index the caps, and use finitely many successive compactifications. Earlier trace, mass and recurrent membership conclusions persist on each refinement.

For an arbitrary fixed point, an index contains it infinitely often along the common subsequence. Its limiting cap contains it, with no full-measure exceptional set. All limiting masses are at most Q. A deepest point is in a member of the cover and forces that member's mass to be at least Q, equivalently the proof's finite-maximum argument.

The anchored predecessor supplies Q and an attaining nonvertical through-point cap at every point, including null fibers. A small outward translation gives ambient interior membership and mass strictly below Q+εM, because εM>0 and the mass converges to the original mass. Compactness gives a finite interior cover.

The complement of each cap interior is a convex closed halfspace. These complements and C have empty intersection on Λ. The primary Helly theorem applies to their restrictions to Λ. If the family has fewer than h members, retain it all. Otherwise an empty subfamily has at most h members. Any point of S belongs to C, so the selected complements cannot all contain it, whether or not C was selected. This gives the desired interior subcover.

Checked the definition (H) and Theorem 1.1(3) in the Averkov–Weismantel primary preprint https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.0948. Its real dimension is d and its integer dimension is n in this application. Equality concerns the Helly number; the candidate's cap count is an upper bound. The limiting conclusion concerns a closed cover of S.

Checked the opening assertion and §§1–2 in archive b989614dc4f86228 at b9df7802ecad0edda8b411a145484010a4b7a695. The source assumes the strict covers as an input and proves the exact closed limit; the frozen version additionally establishes that input in the actual mixed-integer convex setting using the anchored predecessor and the primary Helly theorem.

overlap.comparison: Documents the exact mixed Helly number and proves a lower depth bound. It does not furnish nonvertical caps whose closed union covers S at its actual maximum depth.

In continuous dimension two, its final bridge gives an open subthreshold cover of positive-area fibers and its planar reduction acts on a single fiber. This supplies neither the global mixed Helly count nor the zero-loss closed cover of all fibers.

Gives an approximately balanced active family on a distinguished weighted lattice centerpoint fiber. The hypotheses, covered set, and mass control differ from an exact global cap cover at the maximum depth.

readability: “Complementary caps” means the original caps whose interiors are complements of the selected closed halfspaces. The stated bound is an at-most count.

summary: The strict interior covers yield an exact closed cover, and the mixed-integer convex case admits the required strict covers with at most 2^n(d+1) members.
